content: 1. Monitor the patient's response to antidepressant therapy. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme involved in hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide through the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting the CYP2D6 enzyme. Careful titration of the antidepressant dose is recommended to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose. Monitor the antidepressant response during coadministration with tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) and cobicistat. 3. Darunavir and cobicistat both increase the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Ublituximab may decrease the effects of darunavir due to its immunosuppressive properties, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Both darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Monitor closely. 8. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of upadacitinib by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. Caution is advised when upadacitinib is coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Reduce the valbenazine dose to 40 mg once daily when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 10. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of vamorolone by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing over 50 kg. 11. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of venlafaxine by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 16. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant side effects. If prolonged withholding is necessary, consider initiating a revised regimen without a CYP3A or P-gp inhibitor. 17. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant side effects. If prolonged withholding is necessary, consider initiating a revised regimen without a CYP3A or P-gp inhibitor. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Coadministration with voriconazole is not recommended unless the benefit-risk assessment justifies its use. 20. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vortioxetine by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Darunavir may alter warfarin serum concentrations, either increasing or decreasing them. Monitor INR more frequently if coadministered with inhibitors of CYP3A4, CYP1A2, or CYP2C19, and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 22. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of zileuton by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 23. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of zuranolone by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Reduce the zuranolone dose if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of aliskiren by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Clinical monitoring is recommended upon coadministration with antiarrhythmics. 28. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Coadministration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose. 29. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of amoxapine by inhibiting the CYP2D6 enzyme. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose. Monitor the antidepressant response during coadministration with TCAs and cobicistat. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Avoid coadministration with strong dual inhibitors of CYP3A4 and P-gp. 33. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Reduce the aripiprazole dose by 25%, and by approximately 50% if coadministered with both a CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibitor. 34. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of alpelisib by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Avoid coadministration with alpelisib, as it may increase the risk of toxicities. 35. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. 36. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of afatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Reduce the afatinib daily dose by 10 mg if not tolerated when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. 37. Darunavir decreases the effects of albiglutide due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for serious or life-threatening reactions, such as hypotension. 39. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Monitor closely for potential interactions. 41. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Avoid coadministration, as armodafinil is a CYP3A4 inducer and may decrease cobicistat levels. 42. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of artemether by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely.
